narrative_purpose: Shows the real experiment behind the legend: two trees of different species, a tall sunlit one and a smaller shaded one, growing a few metres apart with roots enmeshed in a shared fungal web, and a faint net flow of carbon travelling from the sunlit tree through the fungus toward the shaded, struggling one along a source-to-sink gradient.
subject: Two trees of clearly different species a few metres apart — one tall and bathed in light, one smaller and in shadow — their root systems below the soil line woven together by a shared web of fine fungal threads. Faint glowing particles trace a directional net flow of carbon from the sunlit tree, down through its roots, across the fungal web, and up into the shaded tree.
scene: A forest-floor cross-section, sunlit canopy gap above the larger tree and shade over the smaller, the rich soil below opened to show the shared mycelial web.
camera: A side-on cross-section view spanning both trees, above and below the soil line.
light: A warm shaft of light on the source tree fading to cool shade on the sink tree; the fungal web and the flowing carbon particles glowing cyan-teal below ground.
palette: Void-indigo soil, muted teal foliage, a single restrained warm light shaft, vivid Pandora cyan on the fungal web and the moving carbon.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate with diagrammatic clarity, hand-painted texture.
detail_level: Crisp on both trees, the root coupling, and the directional flow; surrounding forest dissolving into haze.
composition: Source tree left and taller, sink tree right and smaller, the shared web spanning the lower third, dark margins for labels.
consistency_notes: Earth-science figure in the book's cool palette and from-within glow; keep the flow direction legible left-to-right and leave dark space for callout labels.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no neon UI glow, no cartoon or anime style
